teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Have you ever wondered where human beings came from?" Allow a few learners to share their initial thoughts and ideas.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Ask learners to share any stories or beliefs they have heard about how humans came to be
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Theories of the origin of human beings are correctly described

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explain that scientists have also studied the origin of human beings by looking at evidence like old bones and tools.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Guide a discussion about the visual materials, highlighting key changes in physical features
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Theories of the origin of human beings are correctly described

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Briefly discuss how these early changes eventually led to modern human beings (Homo sapiens).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Older learners can explore the work of paleontologists and archaeologists.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Theories of the origin of human beings are correctly described

teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Theories of the origin of human beings are correctly described

teaching_structure.learning_activities: Work individually or in pairs to arrange the cards in a sequence based on their observations

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Begin by revisiting the question: "Where did human beings come from a very long time ago?"

teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Theories of the origin of human beings are correctly described

teaching_structure.teaching_activities:
Introduce the first category of theories:
Creationism/Religious Beliefs. Share one or two simple, age-appropriate stories
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Listen respectfully to the explanations of Creationism and the Theory of Evolution.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Theories of the origin of human beings are correctly described

teaching_structure.teaching_activities:
Ask learners to draw a simple symbol or picture that represents
one of the ideas about human origins they heard today
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Draw their chosen symbol or picture.  Briefly share their drawing if they feel comfortable
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Theories of the origin of human beings are correctly described

teaching_structure.learning_activities: Present prepared model, attempt quizzes and participate in interview
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Theories of the origin of human beings are correctly described
